propositions: The bugfix-size attestation gate blocks large bug fixes (>150 non-test lines) unless they have a plan-review attestation signed by a principal in the pinned trusted_environments.yaml keyring, making it unsatisfiable for developers whose environments are not pinned.

A developer who passes a local plan review cannot obtain an acceptable attestation because the prod op-cert service has no client in the repo, persists nothing, requires a production secret guard header, and the pinning mechanism is CODEOWNERS-gated so contributors cannot self-serve.

The gate's not-pinned arm returns an affirmative 'mismatch' verdict when the DSSE principal is absent from trusted_environments.yaml, which is in FLAG_VERDICTS and causes the gate to BLOCK even when a genuine plan review was completed and signed.

The criterion was redesigned to gate only on the FACT of a completed, lifecycle-valid, subject-bound plan-review attestation, not on the source of certification, removing the trusted_env_keyring lookup and verify_opcert call from the classifier.

Subject binding (ticket id and kind verification) was re-asserted as an explicit step in the classifier because deleting verify_opcert would have silently dropped it, allowing certs to be replayed across different tickets or kinds.

The fix trades anti-adversary verification (DSSE signature check against a trust root) for anti-sloppiness gating because no trust root exists for unpinned signers, accepting that attestation records on the attacker-writable tickets branch can be fabricated but remaining fail-closed on the real boundary (LLM-Review and Verified votes are bot-only).
